FINAL: Padres 8, Cubs 0

First-inning home runs from Fernando Tatis Jr. and Manny Machado. Seven brilliant one-hit innings from Michael King. This is the Padres team that's played better than anyone in baseball for more than two months. And they put a Game 1 walloping on Chicago.

FINAL: Yankees 9, Red Sox 0

Ben Rice hit two home runs and drove in six. Cam Schlittler threw 6.1 scoreless and struck out 10. New York beat the snot out of Boston and can clinch an ALDS berth against Tampa Bay with a win Wednesday or, if necessary, Thursday.
Ben Rice is 4 for 5 with two home runs and six RBIs. He has as many hits tonight as he did the entire 2025 postseason.
The Red Sox pulled Payton Tolle to give Ben Rice a different look. The look Erik Miller gave him was a middle-middle fastball.

FINAL: White Sox 6, Astros 3

Battle of the bullpen game goes to Chicago, which got three scoreless from rookie Hagen Smith and scored in four of the first five innings. White Sox looking to win their first playoff series since the 2005 World Series and have two chances to do it.

FINAL: Braves 5, Phillies 3

Don Mattingly went to Jhoan Duran in the seventh inning. Austin Riley hit a three-run go-ahead homer off him in the eighth. Philadelphia will try to save its season tomorrow with Cristopher Sánchez. Game 1 winners are 15-1 in wild card series.

Some notes from the individual votes on the Senate bill:
• Sullivan (AK) did not vote
• Tuberville (AL) was the only vote against the Baldwin amendment to reserve many rights to states 
• Paul (KY) was the only vote in favor of his own amendment throwing the whole bill out and making athlete compensation illegal
• Booker’s 1st amendment was mostly along party lines, with Collins (ME) and Hawley (MO) joining the Democrats to increase the maximum student health fund to $200M
• Booker’s 2nd amendment to make coach mobility match athletes was mostly along party lines, with Britt (AL) voting yes and Cantwell (WA) voting no
• Final passage had GOP Senators 50-2 in favor, with Paul (KY) and Scott (FL) opposed. Democrats were 27-20 in favor
